A digital system with three inputs (a, b, c) generates a logic-1 output for binary values 0, 2, 5, and 7, and a logic-0 output for binary values 1, 3, 4, and 6. Determine the output j_sop in minimum sum-of-products form, and the output j_pos in minimum product-of-sums form.

module top_module (
	input a,
	input b,
	input c,
	output j_sop,
	output j_pos);
code:
module top_module (
	input a,
	input b,
	input c,
	output j_sop,
	output j_pos);assign j_sop = (~a & ~b & ~c) | (~a & b & ~c) | (a & ~b & c) | (a & b & c);
assign j_pos = (a | b | ~c) & (a | ~b | c) & (~a | b | c) & (~a | ~b | ~c);
endmodule

description:
The module implements a key generation mechanism for processing metadata based on input signals. It takes a clock signal and a reset signal to manage its operations. When the `p2k_valid` signal is asserted, the module generates output metadata (`k2m_metadata`) depending on the current mode (indicated by the `mode` input) and the `p2k_ingress` value. In mode 1, the output metadata is constructed differently based on whether `p2k_ingress` is zero or not, while in the alternate mode, it uses the `p2k_eid_dst` source. The generated metadata is accompanied by a validity signal (`k2m_metadata_valid`), which indicates whether the output metadata is currently valid. The design essentially serves as a metadata formatter or encoder driven by input criteria, facilitating the generation of contextualized keys or identifiers for further processing.
module top_module(
clk,
reset,
p2k_valid,
p2k_ingress,
p2k_rloc_src,
p2k_eid_dst,
p2k_metadata,

mode, 

k2m_metadata_valid,
k2m_metadata
);

Design a shift register with both serial and parallel input capabilities. The module has a width parameter, allowing for dynamic sizing up to a specified number of bits (default is 8). It takes several control signals: CLOCKENABLE to trigger updates, LATCHINPUTVALUE to load the serial input into the register, and PARALLELLOAD to set the register directly with the serial input. The shift register enables shifting of data based on the state of the least significant bit of the output (Q[0]), allowing for flexible operation in serial or parallel modes. The serial output is derived from the least significant bit of the shift register's contents.
module top_module(CLOCKENABLE, INPUTCLK, LATCHINPUTVALUE, PARALLELLOAD, SERIALIN, SERIALOUT, Q);

Design a memory interface module that performs read and write operations to a 32-bit wide memory array consisting of 1024 entries. It features synchronous operation triggered by a rising clock edge. When the reset_n signal is deasserted (low), the output data is initialized to zero. If the write_en signal is high, the module writes the incoming data_in to the specified address in memory. If write_en is low, it reads the data from the specified address and outputs it on data_out.
module top_module(
    input clk,
    input reset_n,
    input [31:0] data_in,
    input write_en,
    input [14:0] address,
    output reg [31:0] data_out
);
code:
module top_module(
    input clk,
    input reset_n,
    input [31:0] data_in,
    input write_en,
    input [14:0] address,
    output reg [31:0] data_out
);reg [31:0] memory [0:1023];

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!reset_n) begin
        data_out <= 0;
    end else if (write_en) begin
        memory[address] <= data_in;
    end else begin
        data_out <= memory[address];
    end
end

endmodule

description:
Design a one-bit wide, 2-to-1 multiplexer. The output, 'out', is determined by the 'select' signal; when 'select' is 0, 'out' outputs 'input1', and when 'select' is 1, 'out' outputs 'input2'.
module top_module(input1, input2, select, out);

Design a finite state machine (FSM) capable of processing a specified number of input signals and producing outputs based on its current state. This module features parameters to define the number of input signals, output signals, states, and transitions, providing flexibility for different implementations. It utilizes synchronous state transitions triggered by the clock signal and incorporates a reset functionality to initialize the FSM to its starting state. The module manages state transitions and output generation based on the current input and the defined behavior of the FSM, which includes state merging to optimize the design.
module top_module(
  input clk,
  input rst,
  input [n-1:0] in,
  output [m-1:0] out,
  output [log2(s)-1:0] state
);

This is a sequential circuit. Analyze the simulation waveforms to determine the circuit's behavior, then implement it.

Time 0ns: clk = 0, reset = 0, output = 0.
Time 5ns: clk = 1, reset = 0, output = 0.
Time 10ns: clk = 0, reset = 1, output = 0.

Construct a circuit that combines a dual-port RAM with a shift register. The RAM stores 8 words of 4 bits each, allowing read and write operations based on specified addresses. The shift register accepts a single bit of input data and shifts it left on each clock cycle when enabled, producing a 1-bit output. Upon reset, all RAM contents and the shift register are initialized to zero. The RAM outputs the current read data, while the shift register outputs the least significant bit after shifting.
module top_module(
    input clk,
    input rst_n,
    input data_in, // Input data for the RAM and shift register
    input shift_en, // Enable signal for the shift register
    output reg [3:0] shift_out, // Output from the shift register
    output reg [3:0] ram_out // Output from the RAM at the current read address
);

Design a simple one-bit buffer. The output follows the input directly, meaning whenever the input changes, the output updates to match the input value.
module top_module(output reg o, input i);

Implement a Verilog module that toggles its output q every clock cycle if the input t is high. Assume positive edge-triggered clock.

module top_module (
	input clk,
	input t,
	output reg q);

Design a Wishbone bus interface module that supports both read and write operations. This module takes various inputs, including a clock signal, reset signal, and Wishbone control signals, to manage data transactions. It contains a state machine that acknowledges incoming requests, handles data reading and writing, and maintains an output acknowledgment signal. The module features specific address mapping for interrupt generation and manages internal registers to store the address and data for operations. Upon reset, the module initializes its registers to zero and clears acknowledgment and interrupt outputs. When a write operation is detected, it stores the given address and data, whereas, for a read operation, it outputs the stored address.
module top_module(
  input             clk,
  input             rst,
  input             i_wbs_cyc,
  input             i_wbs_stb,
  input      [31:0] i_wbs_adr,
  input      [31:0] i_wbs_dat,
  input             i_wbs_we,
  output reg [31:0] o_wbs_dat,
  output reg        o_wbs_ack,
  output reg        o_wbs_int
);

Implement the Verilog module based on the following description.
A "1-bit NOR gate" circuit outputs the bitwise NOR of two 1-bit input vectors. Build a 1-bit NOR gate circuit.
module top_module (
	input in0,
	input in1,
	output reg out);

description:
Design a 2-entry FIFO (First-In, First-Out) buffer with control signals for reading, writing, and status indicators. The module utilizes two 8-bit wide data storage elements to hold data written from the input `wr_data`. It manages read and write operations with pointers (`wr_ptr` and `rd_ptr`) to track the current position for writing and reading. The design includes outputs for `empty`, `full`, `almost_empty`, and `almost_full` to signal buffer status conditions, and it resets the buffer state upon the active low `reset_n` signal. Data can be written to the buffer when not full and read when not empty, effectively controlling data flow in a structured manner.
module top_module(
  input clk,
  input wr,
  input rd,
  input reset_n,
  input [7:0] wr_data,
  output reg [7:0] rd_data,  // Changed from wire to reg
  output empty,
  output full,
  output almost_empty,
  output almost_full
);

Implement a Verilog module with the following description: Counts the number of ones.
module top_module(input [15:0] vec, output reg [4:0] count);

Design a 64x8-bit RAM module that supports reading and writing operations. The module has inputs for write data, read and write addresses, clock, write enable, read enable, and reset signals. On the rising edge of the clock, if the reset signal is active, the memory is initialized to zero; otherwise, if the write enable is asserted, the module stores the write data at the specified write address. When read enable is active, the output provides the data from the specified read address; if read enable is not active, the output is high-impedance.
module top_module(ReadData, WriteData, Reset,readAddress,writeAddress, Clk, writeEn,readEn);

Design a 4-bit universal shift register with various shifting and loading capabilities. The module takes a 2-bit control signal (S) to determine the operation: no shift (00), right shift (01), left shift (10), or parallel load from the input (11). On a rising clock edge, if the reset signal is high, the output is cleared to zero. Otherwise, the operation specified by S modifies the output register (Q) accordingly, enabling flexible data manipulation within a 4-bit parallel structure.
module top_module(
input [1:0] S,
input [3:0] in,
output reg [3:0] Q,
input clk,
input reset
);

Design a 4-bit adder/subtractor circuit. The circuit takes two 4-bit inputs, A and B, and a control input, SUB. When SUB is low (0), the circuit performs the addition of A and B and outputs the result as SUM. When SUB is high (1), it performs the subtraction of B from A and outputs the result as SUM.
module top_module(A, B, SUB, SUM);

Design a 32-bit Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) that performs various operations based on a 3-bit operation selector (S_Op). The ALU can execute addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, bitwise OR, bitwise AND, and comparison (less than) between two 32-bit inputs (Op1 and Op2). The result of the selected operation is output as R_Op, and a zero flag (ZF) is set to indicate if the result is zero. If an unsupported operation is selected, R_Op is set to an undefined state.
module top_module(
		
		
		input [31:0]Op1,
		input [31:0]Op2,
		input [2:0]S_Op,
		
		output reg ZF,
		output reg[31:0]R_Op
);
